results.name: lxml equivalence: every rewritten XML part of the 353-file corpus + 15 adversarial shapes keeps its expanded names, attributes, text, comments and MCE prefix meanings, in canonical prefixes; Excel's own parts take the no-copy fast path

adversarial shapes read correctly: comment / CDATA / PI lookalikes untouched, no-namespace children undeclare the default, strict prefixes canonical, value text is not a declaration, foreign namespace on the x14 prefix aliased away, x14 as the default namespace becomes x14:, MCE lists follow the renaming

the 7 corpus workbooks TT66 could not read (x: / s: SpreadsheetML prefixes, prefixed mc:AlternateContent) open, and every non-empty cell equals an lxml namespace-aware reader and (where it can open the file) openpyxl; TT66 rejected 6 and read 0 cells from the 7th

x14 conditional formats written under other prefixes (q: for x14, m: for xm) are modelled exactly like Excel's spelling; the MS-XLSX oracle confirms the renamed file is the same x14 content; TT66 lost the x14-only rules
a FOREIGN namespace that borrows the x14 prefix is never read as conditional formatting (TT66 read it as a rule: a false positive)
lossless save of a prefixed workbook: edit one cell of 59021.xlsx (x: prefixes), patch, re-read → the edit and every other value survive; openpyxl opens the result

pre-standard / unknown dialects: the Excel 2007 beta namespace (sample-beta.xlsx) is SpreadsheetML; a workbook in a namespace nobody knows is read exactly as TT66 read it (knownRoot guard) instead of being aliased away
numeric character references are decoded in ONE pass, exactly as an XML parser does (lxml oracle): decimal, hex, astral, newline; &lt; stays the text <; TT66 showed the raw &#…; text

references that are not characters (lone surrogate in hex and decimal, beyond U+10FFFF in hex and decimal) stay literal instead of crashing or inventing a character — lenient, as Excel-tolerant readers are; lxml rejects such files outright

lossless re-style of a cell in an x:-prefixed styles.xml changes ONLY its font (openpyxl): the patcher reads styles through the same canonical view as the reader (found by the TT67 gate: fill / border / alignment were rebuilt)
the x14 oracle REPORTS malformed XML and unreadable packages as findings (TT66 raised a traceback, so a broken writer looked like a broken test)

whole-corpus differential vs the TT66 reader (338 workbooks: cells + styles + CF + tables + charts): nothing reads worse; the only changes are 7 workbooks that now open (6 rejected, 1 read empty) and 3 whose &#…; text is now decoded
cost: Excel-written parts return the SAME string (no copy); a 20 000-row x:-prefixed sheet (≈4 MB) is canonicalised in well under 2 s and reads all 100 000 cells
